dedupe_keys.name: xbrl extensible business reporting language standard

description: XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) is the open data exchange standard for digital business reporting, used by regulators and companies to tag financial statements, prudential returns and sustainability reports so that software can read them. The standard includes the core specifications, Inline XBRL for human- and machine-readable documents, the Open Information Model with CSV and JSON forms, XBRL Global Ledger for transactional reporting and software certification. It is maintained by XBRL International, a not-for-profit consortium of jurisdictions and members, whose Table Constraints specification became a full Recommendation on 10 September 2026; recent news covers the revised European Sustainability Reporting Standards taxonomy and UK reporting reform. Coverage is global. The specifications and guidance are available free online, with tools listed by vendors; the FSB describes XBRL as a freely licensed open standard. Caveats: XBRL defines the format, not the data, and taxonomies differ by regulator, so comparing filings needs mapping. For simulation it is the format in which bank supervisory data, such as EBA reporting and FSB incident reports, are exchanged, so tools that read it open these sources to financial resilience models. It is related to the FSB FIRE taxonomy package and EBA reporting frameworks records in this catalogue.
